staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout, and the line locations below are grounded in this tree. The sample metadata names vulnerable commit `7a588237fdb744e5825fb119753dcad2e8878866`, but the prepared workspace used the commit above.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42488121 (fluent-bit): Heap-buffer-overflow READ {*} found by fuzz target flb-it-fuzz-parser_fuzzer_OSSFUZZ [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42488121
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The staged 100-byte witness is consumed by `parser_fuzzer` as a 7-byte parser-configuration prefix followed by 93 bytes of raw parse input. The first control byte selects the logfmt parser and the sixth enables the harness's fixed typed-key table `{AAA:int, BBB:float, CCC:bool, DDD:string, EEE:hex}`. In the remaining buffer, `logfmt_parser()` later materializes the key/value pair `CCC=Y` directly as bounded slices of the heap-backed testcase; `flb_parser_typecast()` matches `CCC` to the BOOL rule, the single-byte value `Y` fails both boolean conversions, and the cast-error path calls `flb_warn("[PARSER] key=%s cast error. save as string.", key)` on the raw key slice. Because `key` is not NUL-terminated and the witness contains no zero byte from that `CCC` token through the end of the 100-byte allocation, `vsnprintf()` in `flb_log_print()` scans into the redzone and AddressSanitizer reports the saved heap-buffer-overflow read of size 53. The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by copying `key` into `key_len + 1` bytes, appending `\0`, and logging that terminated copy instead.

source.description: First project parser step that turns attacker-controlled logfmt bytes into the bounded `key,key_len` slice later misused as a C string.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 100-byte blob with SHA-256 `1ea06a55f86bb3318ed8ca474ac9df1ac140bc276cf8bef7af2d301d20ca5d03`. The harness consumes bytes 0..6 as parser configuration and passes the remaining 93-byte payload to `flb_parser_do()`. On the crashing logfmt iteration, parser offsets 41..46 / file offsets 48..53 are `43 43 43 3d 59 3d` (`CCC=Y=`), so this step materializes `key = "CCC"` and `key_len = 3` from the heap-backed testcase buffer.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The cast-error handler passes the bounded logfmt key slice directly to `flb_warn(..., "%s", key)` even though `logfmt_parser()` never NUL-terminates that slice.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes this exact obligation by allocating `key_len + 1` bytes, copying `key`, appending `\0`, and logging `nt_key` instead of the raw parser buffer slice.

sink.description: Closest project sink to the ASan crash. `vsnprintf()` consumes the `%s` vararg from `flb_warn()` and scans past the testcase heap buffer because `key` lacks a terminating NUL.
sink.note: The saved trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 53` in `printf_common`, and `flb_log_print /src/fluent-bit/src/flb_log.c:406:13` is the first project frame.

tainted_value_origin.description: The harness consumes a 7-byte configuration prefix and passes the remaining bytes directly into the selected parser. For the staged witness, byte 0 selects `format = "logfmt"`, byte 5 enables the 5-entry typed-key table, and `data,size` at this call describe the 93-byte payload later aliased by `key`.

parser_admitted.description: Project dispatch checkpoint into the vulnerable parser path.
parser_admitted.condition: The first control byte of the staged witness is `0x7b`, so the harness builds the parser with `type == FLB_PARSER_LOGFMT`; byte 5 is `0x27`, so `parser->types_len == 5`. Therefore `flb_parser_do()` routes the remaining 93 bytes into `flb_parser_logfmt_do()` and the later key/value pair is handled by `flb_parser_typecast()` instead of the untyped msgpack path.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness interprets the first 7 testcase bytes as parser configuration, creates a logfmt parser with the fixed typed-key table, and passes the remaining 93 bytes as the raw parse buffer.
On the crashing logfmt iteration, the parser materializes the bounded key slice `CCC` and value slice `Y` directly from the heap-backed testcase and routes them into typed conversion.
The typed-key match selects `CCC`'s BOOL rule, the value `Y` fails the boolean conversion, and the cast-error path logs the raw `key` slice with `%s` instead of a NUL-terminated copy.
`vsnprintf()` formats that unterminated `%s` argument, scans off the right edge of the 100-byte testcase allocation, and triggers the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: The first seven testcase bytes configure the parser before line 145 consumes the remaining input: `data[0] = 0x7b` makes the harness choose `format = "logfmt"`, `data[5] = 0x27` enables the fixed typed-key table `{AAA:int, BBB:float, CCC:bool, DDD:string, EEE:hex}`, and `data[6]` is even so no decoder rewrites occur. After those control bytes are consumed, `data,size` name the 93-byte heap-backed parser payload at file offsets 7..99.

Source. On the iteration that matters, after skipping earlier ordinary pairs and garbage, `key` aliases parser-payload bytes 41..43 / file offsets 48..50, which are the ASCII bytes `43 43 43` (`CCC`), and `key_len = 3`. This slice points directly into the 100-byte fuzz allocation and is bounded only by `key_len`; it is not NUL-terminated.

After the `=` that terminates `CCC`, the unquoted-value branch materializes `value` as the single byte `0x59` (`Y`) and stops immediately at the next `=` byte, so `value_len = 1`. The later BOOL cast therefore receives the slice `Y`, not `true` or `false`.

fine_trace.var: parser->types, parser->types_len, key, key_len, value, value_len
fine_trace.note: Because the harness enabled the type table in step 0, `logfmt_parser()` routes this `CCC=Y` pair into `flb_parser_typecast()` instead of the plain msgpack string path.
The bounded comparison matches the attacker-controlled slice `CCC` against the harness-provided table entry `types[2].key == "CCC"`, so this pair is handled by the `FLB_PARSER_TYPE_BOOL` case.
The single-byte value slice from step 2 is `Y`, so neither boolean-literal comparison succeeds and the BOOL cast fails with `error = FLB_TRUE`.

Root cause. On cast failure, the code forwards the raw key slice to `flb_warn()` as a `%s` argument without first copying `key_len` bytes and appending `\0`. In the staged witness there is no `0x00` byte from the `C` at file offset 48 through file offset 99, so `key` still denotes `CCC=Y=AA...` followed by the rest of the 52 in-bounds trailing bytes when the logger treats it as a C string. The fix inserts a `key_len + 1` copy and explicit terminator before this call.

ASan sink. `vsnprintf()` formats step 6's `%s` argument with C-string semantics, so libc scans from the `key` pointer until a NUL byte is found. Because the 100-byte testcase allocation contains no zero byte after the `CCC` token, `printf_common` reads off the right edge of the heap region; the saved trace reports `READ of size 53` at the first byte past `[0x60b0000001a0, 0x60b000000204)`.

allocation_context.note: The overread target is the 100-byte libFuzzer testcase allocation; the `key` pointer from step 1 is a slice into that heap region.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch null-terminates `key` before the warning call at `src/flb_parser.c:917`, which matches the traced root cause. Stage 02 did not run a fixed build, so this field remains `false`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42488121 run --version vulnerable --expect crash` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 53` with stack `printf_common -> flb_log_print -> flb_parser_typecast -> logfmt_parser -> flb_parser_logfmt_do`, matching OSS-Fuzz issue 42488121.

format.name: 100-byte parser_fuzzer input with a 7-byte configuration prefix and raw logfmt payload
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 100-byte blob stored in `poc` (SHA-256 `1ea06a55f86bb3318ed8ca474ac9df1ac140bc276cf8bef7af2d301d20ca5d03`). Control byte 0 is `0x7b`, so the harness selects `format = "logfmt"`; bytes 1..3 are even, so no time format, time key, or time offset strings are consumed; byte 4 is odd, so `time_keep` is true but irrelevant to the crashing pair; byte 5 is `0x27`, so the fixed typed-key table `{AAA:int, BBB:float, CCC:bool, DDD:string, EEE:hex}` is enabled; and byte 6 is even, so no decoder rewrites occur. The remaining 93-byte parser payload contains the bytes `43 43 43 3d 59 3d` (`CCC=Y=`) at parser offsets 41..46 / file offsets 48..53, and there is no `0x00` byte from that `C` through EOF. In the vulnerable source this exact combination makes `CCC` hit the BOOL cast, forces `error = FLB_TRUE`, and passes the unterminated `key` slice to `flb_warn("...%s...", key)`, reproducing the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow read. Stage 01 only proves this exact 100-byte witness and observed path; this contract does not generalize to neighboring parser-control bytes or other logfmt payloads.
